rv.q: Minor gripes aside Ms HSB has the chutzpah to deliver a yarn with confidence albeit the material would benefit from a slower and clear narrative arc.
Yet you may end up feeling a little short-changed by Santa Barnes’s central creation.
Honor Santa Barnes delivers a remarkable performance full of attitude and energy.
As it is, this is a great show: bold, funny and compelling.
Florence is entertaining, intelligent, and thought-provoking, made distinct by Honor Santa Barnes's versatility as both a writer and a performer.
It is funny, disarming, and occasionally disturbing, and is certainly helped by Honor's personable performance...
This play about many personalities doesn’t have many things to say.
Instead of critiquing the affluent upper class Florence is from, Barnes only highlights its silliness.
The show gets more interesting when it's not about Florence and ironically you never feel you get to know Florence very well, she's a hollow cipher – a blank canvas even.

cn.t: Critics are divided on Florence, Honor Santa Barnes' one-woman art world satire. Most praise her sharp script and energetic performance, though some find the messaging muddled. A Fringe hit that largely translates to the stage.
